output.summary: Approved G1028 design revision 2: (1) an agent or human reviewer's open finding stays live while its target's output still matches, even after the review goes stale (goal edits no longer drop findings); the target's card marks them stale_review and edit previews carried_findings with waive lines; lens findings follow the filter's last verdicts. (2) Review cards list only open findings in previous.findings, resolved ones under previous.resolved; restating resolved is a no-op, restating open on a closed id is refused 'already resolved'. (3) `follows: <id>` links a new finding to a resolved prior one, inheriting rounds but never upheld; ships as capability finding_follows (G1027), refused until required. (4) Global --repo DIR on worker-facing commands, and the not-a-repository error names the directory. Review approved after one round of two findings.

responses.review_design:1:1: fixed: follows ships as G1027 capability finding_follows (engine/capabilities/finding_follows.txt, added to SHIPPED when G1027 has merged). Submit refuses follows until the required set (requires plus legacy_caps(min)) contains it. The rollout pushes zzzops/policy/requires-finding_follows before the first follows is written, and output_schema mentions follows only when it is required. Both merge orders are stated: if G1028 merges first it uses the next-minor engine.min, which G1027 maps in LEGACY_VERSIONS and converts to the capability. No dependency edge. The §4 table, §9 (SPEC §4.5), the HISTORY row and D8 are updated (§6a).
responses.review_design:1:2: fixed: a follows finding inherits rounds only and is always upheld: false. The follow-up of an upheld finding (rounds >= 2) therefore goes to the human as a dispute item at once, with its new text. §3.3, D5 and test 9 are updated, and new test 9a covers it.

output.summary: Revision 2. Open findings stay live while their review is stale and their target's output is unchanged, marked stale_review, and the edit preview lists every carried finding with waive lines. Closed ids move to previous.resolved: a restated resolved is a no-op, and restating open gives 'already resolved'. New findings may carry follows, inheriting rounds but never upheld. Follows ships as the G1027 capability finding_follows, with a submit gate and both merge orders covered. Worker commands carry a global --repo flag.

findings.text: F1: section 6 rolls out the stored finding key  by raising engine.min, as G1022 D9 did. G1027 (approved, blob 0c556c2) replaces ENGINE_VERSION/engine.min with declared capabilities, and its section 3.6 rule covers new record and finding keys; it has already moved G1022 to capability . 'Only the new engine accepts it in submit' does not protect an old build in another clone. Fix: name a capability (e.g. finding_follows), ship engine/capabilities/<name>.txt in this PR (and add it to G1027's SHIPPED pin), make the rollout push zzzops/policy/requires-<name> before the first follows is written, state both merge orders against G1027 as G1027 section 5 does for G1022, and update the section 4 row and the section 9 contract-edit list (SPEC 4.5).

F2: section 3.3 makes a new finding with follows inherit  from the followed one. upheld means the human sided with the reviewer on that text: the target cannot dispute it (records.check_responses) and it never escalates (frontier.escalates). Inheriting it lets a reviewer attach freely written new demands that neither the target nor the human can push back on, which weakens the dispute safeguard. Fix: inherit rounds as designed (so resolve-and-follow cannot dodge escalation), but always set upheld false on the new finding, so a dispute at rounds >= 2 escalates to the human. Update section 3.3, D5 and test 9, and add a test that a follow of an upheld finding is disputable and escalates.

output.summary: Revision 2 resolves both findings. `follows` ships as G1027 capability `finding_follows`, with a submit gate on the required set and both merge orders covered. `follows` inherits `rounds` only, with `upheld` always false, so a follow-up of an upheld finding goes to the human with its new text. The carried_findings preview now lists every carried finding. No new findings, no owner questions.

spec:
Found by several workers while dogfooding Release 1 (2026-11-01):
1. Findings vanish after a goal edit (dogfood 29, 47). Editing G1022's spec after review_design raised 4 findings made the review stale; the reopened design card had `corrections: []`, so the designer saw the findings only because the root relayed them, and the engine has no `fixed:`/`disputed:` response for them. A spec or depends_on edit must not silently drop open findings: keep them live as corrections (marked as from a stale review), or require them to be waived in the edit, and show them on the next card.
2. Restating an already-resolved finding is refused (dogfood 46, hit twice). The reviewer card's `previous.findings` lists resolved findings next to open ones with no flag, `output_schema` says to give a status for "every prior open finding", and submitting a status for a resolved id fails with `unknown finding ids`. Mark resolved ones on the card (or leave them out), accept a restated `resolved`, and say "already resolved" in the refusal.
3. A partly fixed finding has no status (dogfood 44): only open or resolved exist, so a reviewer resolves it and raises a new finding with no link back. Add a link (e.g. `follows: <id>` on a new finding), shown on cards and approval items.
4. Commands need a working directory (dogfood 42, hit by four workers): `submit` and `renew` fail with "not inside a Git repository" outside the repository, and cards' commands carry no cwd. Add `cwd` to card commands, or let the CLI locate the repository from the lease, and make the error say which directory to use.

Acceptance: engine tests for each item (an edit after a changes_requested review keeps the findings on the next card; a restated resolved id is accepted or refused with "already resolved"; `follows` round-trips; a card command runs from outside the repository or the error names the directory). This PR edits docs/design for its contract changes and adds a HISTORY §4 row (G1017's rule).
title: Keep findings and their status straight across review rounds and goal edits
